summary: Junko Matsumura is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed an MA at Australian National University by 1980 and a doctoral dissertation at the University of Göttingen by 1990, later serving as professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2011).
Junko Minamoto is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Ryukoku University and Otani University (circa 1973–1977), and held a research post at Kansai University.

Junmai Zhang worked in philosophy and Sinology. He studied under Qichao Liang (circa 1903–1906) and at Waseda University (circa 1906–1910) and the University of Berlin (circa 1913–1915). He later held posts at Peking University and Tsinghua University.

Junsho Kato worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from the University of Tokyo by 1986. He studied under Akira Hirakawa, Étienne Lamotte, Juntaka Kato, and Hajime Nakamura, and held professorships at Nishogakusha University, Nagoya University, and Reitaku University.

Juntaro Ishihama worked in Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kansai University from circa 1906 to 1908 and later held academic posts at Kansai University (circa 1925–1961) and Ryukoku University.
Junzo Inagaki worked in Buddhist studies. He studied under Shoshin Fukihara and served as a section head at Otani University Library.

Junzo Tanizawa is a philosophy scholar who taught Kei Kataoka. He served as a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 1987) and as an assistant professor at Shinshu University (attested 2000).
Juri Lotman worked in linguistics and related fields. He studied at the University of Saint Petersburg between 1939 and 1961 and took up a post at the University of Tartu in 1954.

Shigeaki (Juro) Watanabe worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Gerhard Oberhammer and held posts at the University of Tsukuba (attested 1989–1990) and as professor at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003).
Jushu Nakasone is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He held posts as a part-time lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 2005) and at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).

Justin McDaniel works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He has served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 2011–2018).

Justin Ritzinger works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett, and held posts at Dharma Drum Mountain, Dharma Drum Buddhist College, Academia Sinica, and Oberlin College.
Justin Shimeld is a philosopher. He completed his PhD at the University of Tasmania (attested 2012) under the supervision of Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.
Justus Günther Grassmann studied at the University of Halle from circa 1797 to 1801 and held a post at the Marienstiftsgymnasium from 1806 to 1852.

Justus Olshausen worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Kiel, Berlin, and Paris under Silvestre de Sacy, Langlès, and Kieffer. His posts included professor and curator at Kiel, professor at Königsberg, and Prussian ministry counselor.
Jyotirindranath Tagore worked in linguistics and other fields. He received his education at Hindu School and at Presidency University around 1864.

János Szerb was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (circa 1975–1980) and held posts at the University of Vienna (1982) and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (circa 1983–1988).

Jérôme Ducor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Jacques May (circa 1985–1993) and held posts at the University of Lausanne (circa 1999–2019) and the International Association of Buddhist Studies (treasurer circa 2002–2014).

Józef Maria Bocheński was a philosopher who studied at Jagiellonian University, the University of Fribourg, and the Pontifical University of Saint Thomas Aquinas. He held posts at the Pontifical University of Saint Thomas Aquinas (circa 1934–1940) and Fribourg (circa 1945–1972).

Józef Szczepan Kowalewski worked in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Vilnius and Kazan under Groddeck, Khalfin, Erdmann, Kazembek, and Igumnov, and held professorships at Kazan Federal University (1833–1860) and the University of Warsaw.
